sentences.text: Author: T. Vinod Kumar Bench: T. Vinod Kumar  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE T. VINOD KUMAR  WRIT PETITION No.2254 OF 2011 ORDER:
Heard learned Counsel for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondent and perused the record.

2. The case of the petitioners, in brief, is that aggrieved by the Award dated 20.02.1981, the petitioners had approached the respondent authority and submitted statement of claim on 28.02.1981 and thereafter also filed an application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (for short 'the Act') seeking reference of the Award passed to the Court, as petitioners are aggrieved by the compensation amount awarded thereunder; and that inspite of the respondent receiving the aforesaid application, the same has not been referred to the Court for proper determination of the compensation amount, which action it is contended is highly illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the scheme of the Act.

3. Per contra, learned Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondent while not disputing that the Award having been passed on 20.02.1981 would however submit that the representation filed by the petitioner on 28.02.1981 cannot be considered as an application under Section 18 of the Act for being it referred to the Court.

4. Learned Government Pleader further submits that since the petitioners had received the compensation amount under the Award, they cannot submit an application under Section 18 of the Act seeking reference to the Court for enhanced compensation inasmuch as the compensation amount has been received without any protest or demur.
5. I have taken note of the respective contentions urged.

6. This Court in W.P. No.17923 of 2024 and also in similar other matters having regard to the law laid down by the Supreme Court in Ajit Singh v. State of Punjab 1 wherein it was held that filing of an application for reference under Section 18 of the Act would by itself manifest the intention of the party and thus, the protest against the Award of the Collector is implied, notwithstanding the acceptance of compensation, had directed the Land Acquisition Officer in those cases to make a 1 (1994) 4 SCC 67 reference of the application filed under Section 18 of the Act to the Court within a period of six weeks.

sentences.text: Since, in the facts of the present case also, as the petitioners have submitted application under Section 18 of the Act on 20.04.1981 and the said application being within the time prescribed under the Act, this Court is of the view that the respondent authority is to be directed to make a reference of the application of the petitioner dated 20.04.1981 to the Court in a time bound manner.

8. Accordingly, the respondent is hereby directed to make reference of the application made by the petitioners dated 20.04.1981 under Section 18 of the Act to the Court within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
9. Subject to the above direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this Writ Petition shall stand closed.
T. VINOD KUMAR, J Date: 11.11.2024 MRKR P. Krishna Niranjan, Warangal Dist.
